question: What is the primary goal of psychiatric rehabilitation leave policies?

options.A: To provide a controlled bridge between institutional care and community living
options.B: To reduce hospital running costs by keeping beds empty
options.C: To punish patients who violate ward regulations
options.D: To permanently discharge chronic psychiatric patients without follow-up

explanation: Structured leave policies allow patients to gradually reintegrate into society while maintaining a connection to the treatment facility. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why are abrupt discharges generally discouraged in favor of phased leave policies?

options.A: Families rarely have transport money on short notice
options.B: Doctors require extended paperwork for immediate releases
options.C: Government regulations prohibit direct discharges from inpatient units
options.D: Abrupt discharges frequently trigger relapse and institutional trauma

explanation: Gradual transitions give patients time to adapt to external stressors and reduce the shock of leaving a structured environment. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h1)

question: What is the typical duration of an occasional leave for a psychiatric patient?

options.A: Exactly six months with weekly renewals
options.B: A few hours up to a weekend
options.D: One full year of community living

explanation: Occasional leaves are brief, temporary absences designed for short visits rather than long-term community reintegration. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h2)

question: What is a major clinical objective of granting occasional leave?

options.A: To permanently evaluate if the family home is suitable for full-time residence
options.B: To test new antipsychotic drug dosages without hospital monitoring
options.C: To test the patient's coping mechanisms and impulse control in a real-world setting
options.D: To clear crowded psychiatric wards during public holidays

explanation: Short-term leaves provide a safe window to observe how well the patient manages brief exposures to family and community stressors. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h2)

question: How does trial leave differ primarily from occasional leave?

options.A: Trial leave requires the patient to stay inside the hospital during nights
options.B: Occasional leave is only for patients with severe cognitive impairment
options.C: Occasional leave requires court approval while trial leave does not
options.D: Trial leave lasts much longer and simulates independent community living

explanation: Trial leave extends over weeks or months to evaluate sustained stability, whereas occasional leave is short-term. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h3)

question: What is a key objective of placing a patient on trial leave?

options.A: To evaluate long-term medication adherence and family resilience
options.B: To force the family to take over full financial responsibility
options.C: To determine if the patient requires an increase in physical restraints
options.D: To immediately terminate hospital liability for the patient's actions

explanation: Extended trial periods help uncover whether the patient and caregivers can sustain stability over time outside institutional walls. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which clinical sign is essential before approving a patient for psychiatric leave?

options.A: Successful graduation from vocational training programs
options.B: Ability to pay all outstanding hospital utility bills
options.C: Complete absence of active homicidal or suicidal ideation
options.D: Complete recovery from all chronic physical illnesses

explanation: Safety is paramount; patients experiencing active self-harm or aggressive impulses are not safe candidates for community leave. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h4)

question: A patient with schizophrenia has been stable on oral medications for two weeks, but still hears command hallucinations telling him to harm others. What is the most appropriate nursing action regarding leave?

options.A: Withhold leave and report the ongoing command hallucinations to the team
options.B: Approve a weekend occasional leave to test if family presence distracts him
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately to reduce ward congestion
options.D: Grant trial leave but instruct the family to lock him in a room at night

explanation: Active command hallucinations targeting others present a severe safety risk, making any form of leave clinically contraindicated. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h4)

question: Why is pre-leave family counseling a critical nursing responsibility?

options.A: It guarantees that the community will provide monthly financial stipends
options.B: It teaches family members how to administer intramuscular injections
options.C: It legally transfers all financial debts of the patient to the relatives
options.D: It helps dispel stigma, explains early relapse signs, and sets realistic expectations

explanation: Involving and educating families prepares them to manage behavioral changes and reduces unhelpful reactions that could trigger relapse. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT an objective of family preparation before patient leave?

options.A: Educating caregivers on recognizing early relapse indicators
options.B: Reducing negative expressed emotion within the household
options.C: Teaching family members how to perform psychiatric diagnostic evaluations
options.D: Establishing a clear emergency contact protocol

explanation: Families are taught to recognize warning signs and support compliance, but formal psychiatric diagnosis remains the duty of trained clinicians. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h5)

question: How should a nurse safely manage medication supply for a patient going on a weekend occasional leave?

options.A: Dispense drugs in secure, labeled containers with precise dosing instructions
options.B: Allow the patient to manage pill distribution without family oversight
options.C: Give the patient a three-month bulk supply to foster total independence
options.D: Instruct the family to purchase all medications from local open-market vendors

explanation: Controlled supply prevents accidental or intentional overdose while ensuring the patient maintains the prescribed therapeutic regimen. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is a primary safety assessment nurses must perform before approving any community leave?

options.A: Verifying the distance between the home and the nearest market
options.B: Assessing the patient's ability to pay private hospital consultation fees
options.C: Checking if the patient owns a functional mobile phone
options.D: Evaluating self-harm potential, flight risk, and medication compliance history

explanation: Assessing risks of self-harm, aggression, and elopement ensures the safety of both the patient and the community during the absence. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is a common method nurses use to monitor a patient during trial leave?

options.A: Scheduled outpatient clinic visits and telephone check-ins
options.B: Installing CCTV cameras in the patient's bedroom
options.C: Requiring daily written police reports from the family
options.D: Sending a security guard to stay in the home full-time

explanation: Routine check-ins and clinic visits allow nurses to track progress and catch emerging problems early without invading privacy. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h7)

question: Why is establishing a liaison with local primary healthcare clinics important during extended trial leave?

options.A: It provides nearby professional support and emergency access for the patient and family
options.B: It ensures the local clinic takes over all legal liability from the main hospital
options.C: It forces the family to pay local taxes to support mental health services
options.D: It replaces the need for any future psychiatric follow-up appointments

explanation: Local primary health centers offer a accessible safety net for caregivers who live far from the main psychiatric facility. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h7)

question: How should a multidisciplinary team interpret a patient's unsuccessful trial leave resulting in symptom relapse?

options.A: As definitive proof that the patient can never live in the community
options.B: As evidence that family counseling was unnecessary and harmful
options.C: As valuable clinical data indicating areas that need further stabilization
options.D: As a disciplinary infraction requiring revocation of all future privileges

explanation: A failed leave identifies specific triggers and treatment gaps, guiding future care adjustments rather than closing the door on rehabilitation. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h8)

question: What is the primary indicator that suggests a patient is ready to move from trial leave to permanent discharge?

options.A: Persistent demands from relatives to empty the hospital bed
options.B: Sustained stability, good medication adherence, and successful coping during leave
options.C: Expiration of the legal time limit allowed for psychiatric hospitalization
options.D: Complete weight restoration and normal vital signs

explanation: Successful trial performance demonstrates that the patient can manage daily life and treatment regimens outside the hospital. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h8)
